title: NETCONF lock semantics: what the RFC doesn't warn you about
excerpt: RFC 6241 describes the lock operation in two paragraphs. Production experience adds about twenty caveats. Here are the ones that cost me a weekend.

title: AI's big bet: who really wins from the data centre boom?
excerpt: Data centres are reshaping power grids, communities and labour markets. Record revenues coexist with layoffs. Environmental justice advocates, nuclear proponents and policy researchers all have something to say about who benefits.

title: Learning Zig with AI-assisted experiments
excerpt: Inspired by a Zig talk, I used AI to bootstrap a set of small hands-on examples, then refined them manually. Notes on what worked, what AI helped with, and why Zig feels practical.

title: AI-generated HTML games: Tetris and Bomberman in a single file
excerpt: Asking an AI to produce self-contained HTML games — no frameworks, no build step. The results for Tetris and a Bomberman clone are playable and illustrate what current models can produce in a single shot.

title: GitBook CI: injecting code snippets automatically with GitHub Actions
excerpt: A Python script and GitHub Actions workflow that scan all markdown files and inline referenced source files before publication — keeping docs and code in sync without manual copy-paste.

title: OTP 29 new features: comprehensions, shuffle, ANSI and native records
excerpt: A demo module covering the headline OTP 29 additions — multi-valued comprehensions (EEP-78), rand:shuffle/1, io_ansi terminal sequences, and the experimental native records feature (EEP-79). Plus kerl workflow for version management.

title: An Erlang OTP release portal: supervision, parsing and view layers
excerpt: A walkthrough of the release_portal rebar3 application — how the supervisor tree is structured, how the parser and logic modules separate concerns, and what the view layer is responsible for.

title: Code analysis with LangChain and TreeSitter: splitting Erlang and Elixir
excerpt: TreeSitter gives you a real AST; LangChain wraps it for RAG pipelines. This PoC shows how to split Erlang and Elixir source into semantically meaningful chunks and feed them to a language model.

title: Network interfaces in C: stb_ds dynamic arrays and stb_sprintf
excerpt: Using the STB single-file C headers to build a network-interface model with dynamic arrays of sub-interfaces and VLANs. Includes a tree-style printer and string-formatting examples.

title: DHCP configuration modelling in C with STB single-file headers
excerpt: Mapping a YANG DHCP model to a C data structure using stb_ds — dynamic arrays with fixed string lengths for embedded-system constraints. Two implementations: fixed strings and char pointers.

title: GPT-5 generated: an Erlang Todo App with SQLite and inets
excerpt: A complete rebar3 OTP application generated by GPT-5: SQLite storage via esqlite, HTTP API with mod_esi, JSON with the built-in OTP 27+ json module, and a small HTML UI — all from a single prompt.

title: Simulating intermittent networks: Docker, HAProxy and tc
excerpt: A Docker Compose setup with a Postgres primary/replica cluster, HAProxy load balancer and three clients. Uses iproute2 tc to inject 20% packet loss between specific services — three scenarios, all scriptable.

title: PostgreSQL ltree: exporting hierarchical data to XML
excerpt: A generic plpgsql function that walks an ltree-structured table and produces nested XML, parameterised by start node and depth. Fully containerised with Docker and testable with make test.

title: XML entity resolution with xmllint: co-located and external variables
excerpt: Two patterns for managing XML variables without a full template engine — co-located entity definitions at the top of the file, and external entity files resolved with xmllint at build time.

title: GSL: teaching Gemini to generate C structs from XML
excerpt: The Generator Scripting Language by iMatix turns XML entity definitions into any target language. Here I teach Gemini about GSL and let it produce a working C struct generator — Makefile and all.

title: AI-assisted diagram creation: from image to Mermaid
excerpt: Giving Gemini an architecture diagram and asking it to produce Mermaid syntax. The result is version-controllable, diff-friendly and good enough for technical documentation.

title: Erlang Fibonacci: the tail-recursive iterator pattern
excerpt: A clean Erlang idiom for the Fibonacci sequence — tail-recursive, using an accumulator pair, and a good template for integer iteration in functional code.
